answer: Because the marble index resolves every citation against the horizon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the terrace audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 28 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 28 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 1114 identities would post 4421 proofs and burn roughly 26 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
